summary: Parboiled rice stir-fried with carrots, green beans, peas and sweetcorn, with a savoury curry and thyme flavour, a party staple beside jollof.
story: Nigerian fried rice is a festive dish served at weddings, holidays and big gatherings, often alongside jollof rice, chicken and plantain. It is made by parboiling rice in seasoned stock, then stir-frying it with diced vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the chicken stock
steps.text: Boil chicken with onion, thyme, a cube and salt for 25 minutes until cooked. Remove the chicken and keep the stock, measuring about 4 cups for the rice.

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice in warm water 2 to 3 times to remove excess starch, which helps keep the grains separate.

steps.title: Parboil the rice
steps.text: Bring the stock to a boil with the curry powder and thyme. Add the rice and boil for 12 to 15 minutes, until it is about 80 percent cooked: a grain should have a firm white centre when bitten. Drain in a sieve and run through with warm water.

steps.title: Steam briefly
steps.text: Return the rice to the pot, cover tightly and leave over the lowest heat for 5 minutes so the grains finish cooking and dry out, then spread to cool slightly.

steps.title: Fry the vegetables
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan. Fry the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the carrots and green beans and cook 3 minutes. Add the peas, sweetcorn and pepper, and stir-fry another 2 minutes so they stay bright and a little crisp.

steps.title: Add liver or shrimp
steps.text: If using, add diced liver or shrimp and stir-fry for about 3 minutes until just cooked through and no longer pink.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the rice to the pan and toss over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes with a seasoning cube, crushed. Add salt to taste. The rice should be colourful, loose and fragrant. Serve with chicken and plantain.

tips: Avoid overcooking the rice. Mushy rice stir-fries into clumps.
Cut vegetables small and evenly for the classic look.
Use a wide pan for tossing. Cooking too much in a deep pot leads to steam, not fry.
Spread cooked rice on a tray if you have time. Cooler, drier rice fries better.

swaps.swap: Basmati or any long-grain rice works. Cook it a little less since it softens faster.
Use stock cubes dissolved in water if you do not have time to boil chicken.
Use extra shrimp, or omit for a vegetarian version made with vegetable stock.

name: Nigerian Fried Rice
